scope: Proposition 4.10 (Gap count and vertex quotients) of the manuscript “Arithmeticity of twisted finite correspondences for lattices over local fields” (preprints/Arithmeticity-of-twisted-finite-correspondences-for-lattices-over-local-fields-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 286 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b1d070a5c4cd8496), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 34. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: In one measured copy, every positive stratum of a source path toward a face of type I has at most |I| infinite gaps. A vertex path has exactly one infinite gap. In a successive single-gap lex chain starting at a vertex, the stage with k source gaps has exactly k target gaps; in particular each such extension adds exactly one. For a quotient of a faster and a slower vertex translation in a common apartment, there is exactly one target gap if the two source vertices are coaxial, and at least two if they are not. Here coaxial means equal or opposite vertices on the same translation axis.
